prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Talk & Command Your Companion", "Press Alt+Space or talk aloud to command your companion."]
1: ["Review Your Companion's Look", "Verify lighting and features before finalizing your companion."]
2: []
3: ["Choose Your Pet's Journey", "Select whether you want to adopt a ready pet or craft a custom companion."]
4: ["Log into your existing account to restore previously adopted desktop pets seamlessly."]
5: ["Your Pet is Ready! Press Ctrl+Shift+H to Hide or Show Anytime", "Your companion lives on your desktop. Use Ctrl+Shift+H whenever you want to toggle visibility or right-click for options."]
6: ["Name Your New Desktop Companion"]
7: ["Your pet is being crafted. You can minimize this window; we will alert you when ready."]
8: ["Upload Clear JPG or PNG Photos", "For best results, upload well-lit photos facing forward. Avoid heavy filters or covered faces."]
9: ["Includes Free Starter Desktop Decor"]

verdicts.problem: Asks for personal photos of the user
